description: Bodies for Al Jazeera, WE News and the retrospective Afghan Witness report were reviewed. The first two repeat a Purple Saturdays account; Afghan Witness adds investigative coverage but was published after Q1 and its underlying video and cited media reports were not independently inspected. There is no systematic archive-equivalent search, and comprehensive open-web coverage or independent event-level confirmation is not established.
required_followup: Continue date- and location-bounded searches and verify relevant independent source bodies after fresh per-attempt gate and manual review; preserve inaccessible archive gaps and verify underlying evidence only through fresh source-specific checks.

description: The two March 8 press reports anchor the Takhar/Balkh actions to that date and mention a separate Mazar-i-Sharif event on Thursday. The April 10 Afghan Witness retrospective says IWD online activity began March 1 and describes March 8 actions, but does not establish street-action onset before March, continuation after March, or movement continuity across month boundaries.
required_followup: Search adjacent months and use further permitted source bodies to establish whether these local actions were isolated, connected or part of a continuing episode; do not count the February duplicate as a February event.

description: Al Jazeera and WE News describe the Takhar/Balkh actions in private settings, giving seven in Takhar and “several/a few” in Balkh; WE News reports no public protests by Friday afternoon. The separate Mazar event had about 20. The April Afghan Witness report retrospectively records indoor actions reportedly in Kabul, Takhar and Balkh and one outdoor Taloqan march, but gives no attendance totals or public-access conditions. Its Taloqan clip shows no other people or cars, which does not establish participant count. No source establishes an individual gathering of 50 or more.
required_followup: Seek independent event-specific evidence for each gathering’s attendance and venue/access conditions, including geolocation and count for the Taloqan video; keep Mazar separate unless evidence links it to a qualifying protest.

description: Al Jazeera and WE News attribute the activist account to Purple Saturdays and repeat similar Takhar/Balkh details, so they are not independent event confirmation. The April Afghan Witness report is a separate investigative publication and reports its own monitoring of videos and ten movements, but its linked footage and cited media reports were not inspected; the Taloqan location attribution and underlying evidence remain unverified.
required_followup: Compare further permitted bodies and independently inspect relevant underlying sources only after fresh source-specific gate/manual review; do not infer event-level independence from different domains or organizational labels.
